prompt: What kind of cable is used to charge an iPhone?
response:
To charge an iPhone, you typically use a Lightning cable. The Lightning connector was introduced with the iPhone 5s and was used for charging and data transfer until the iPhone 12 series, when Apple transitioned to the MagSafe charging system. However, for charging older iPhones, a Lightning to USB-C cable or a Lightning to USB cable is necessary.

For newer iPhones (starting from the iPhone 12 series), you can use a MagSafe charging cable, which is a magnetic charging system that also includes a MagSafe adapter for wireless charging and accessories like the MagSafe cases and clips.

If you have an iPhone 8 or later, you can use a Lightning to USB-C cable to charge your device. If you have an iPhone 7 or earlier, you can use a Lightning to USB cable.

Always ensure that the cable you use is compatible with your iPhone model and that it is from a trusted source to avoid any potential damage to your device.
